data.title: PM caught handing out cash to flood victims
data.description: Sparking online debate after being captured on a Facebook live stream , Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul was seen handing out cash to flood-hit residents of communities in Bangkok's Sai Mai district late on Tuesday.

data.title: Bangkok's City Hall reports flooding on about 10 roads
data.description: The Drainage and Sewerage Department of the Bangkok Metropolitan Administration (BMA) reported flooding on about 10 roads in the capital on Wednesday morning, with water levels ranging from seven to 20 centimetres.

data.title: Bangkok opens shelter for animals rescued from floodwaters
data.description: Dogs and cats displaced by severe flooding in Bangkok can now receive temporary shelter, health assessments and medical care at the Prawet Animal Shelter, the Bangkok Metropolitan Administration (BMA) announced on Wednesday.

data.title: Radio waves coming from an alien planet may be a cosmic first
data.description: NEW YORK — Radio waves streaming from an alien planet may offer a new tool in the hunt for life elsewhere in the universe.

data.title: Thieves swipe drugs under nose of Fiji police, swap with flour
data.description: SYDNEY — Detectives were sifting leads Wednesday after a massive drug heist in Fiji, searching for dozens of cocaine parcels swiped from an evidence vault and replaced with baking flour.

data.title: Singha R-SA & Rescue Networks Expand Flood Relief Across Bangkok, Rayong & Prachin
data.description: Singha R-SA has continued providing assistance to flood victims for the fifth consecutive day, deploying teams across several areas of Bangkok and working with rescue networks to evacuate residents in Rayong and Prachin Buri provinces.

data.title: North Korea denies South's claim it was apparently behind DMZ mine blasts
data.description: SEOUL — The powerful sister of North Korean leader Kim Jong Un denied a South Korean claim that North Korea was apparently behind landmine blasts last week that injured three soldiers, state media reported Wednesday.

data.title: West Bank's violent settlers part of a new generation fuelled by ideology
data.description: JERUSALEM — A mass attack by Israeli settlers on a Palestinian village in the occupied West Bank has placed new focus on the emergence of a generation of radicals in the territory.

data.title: Myanmar arrests 21 over alleged donations to opposition-linked fundraising platform
data.description: NAY PYI TAW — Myanmar's military-backed government has arrested 21 people it said ​had transferred money to an online ‌fundraising platform linked to the opposition National Unity Government (NUG), the state-run Global New Light of Myanmar newspaper reported.

data.title: New Zealand denies breaching climate commitments to EU
data.description: WELLINGTON - New Zealand denied on Wednesday it had broken climate promises made in a free-trade deal with the European Union (EU), after a green group lodged a complaint with Brussels.

data.title: US Supreme Court lifts limits on third-country deportations
data.description: WASHINGTON — The United States Supreme Court on Tuesday lifted restrictions on the deportations of immigrants to countries that are not their own, while agreeing to hear the issue on its merits in December.

data.title: Paw-fect candidate: Australia finds new koala rescue dog
data.description: SYDNEY — After trawling through dozens of applications, the hunt is over: an Australian animal welfare group has found a successor to a hero hound credited with saving more than 100 koalas from fires.

data.title: Mars Impact Fund Commits $3M to Worldwide Veterinary Service for Rabies Elimination in Thailand
data.description: On World Rabies Day, Mars, Incorporated is celebrating a partnership with Worldwide Veterinary Service (WVS) to support final-mile rabies elimination in Thailand. The partnership is supported by a $3M philanthropic grant awarded through the Mars Impact Fund, which is focused on strengthening sourcing community resilience, developing the next generation of scientists and improving companion animal wellbeing.

data.title: Pirate island's plunging population shows Greece's demographic decline
data.description: THYMAINA — "Let's go to war!" shouted six-year-old Giorgos at his older cousin, Minas, as the two chased each other with claw-like geranium stalks around the schoolyard on the tiny Greek island of Thymaina.

data.title: Women fight fires and sexism in Indonesian Borneo
data.description: KETAPANG — Housework in the morning followed by several hours of firefighting: women in Indonesian Borneo risk life and limb to battle blazes making their communities sick, all while shouldering a sexist backlash.

data.title: US-led coalition ends mission in Iraq
data.description: ERBIL — After more than a decade, the US-led coalition is ending its mission in Iraq, having helped save the country from jihadists while causing persistent friction.

data.title: Thai Hotels Association expects floods to cut Bangkok hotel occupancy by less than 10% in Sept–Oct
data.description: Bangkok's floods could deter Chinese visitors ahead of Golden Week on October 1, as tourism groups call for clear updates and lasting solutions

data.title: Seed rights split growers from farmers
data.description: Thailand is preparing to discuss adopting UPOV 1991 with the European Union as part of free trade negotiations next month, with the proposed rules drawing support from seed producers but opposition from farmer groups concerned about restrictions on seed saving and exchange.

data.title: Molly gets 20th birthday show from Pop Mart Thailand at CU
data.description: Chulalongkorn University Centenary Park is the venue for world-class international art toy show "Molly 20th Anniversary Exhibition - Bangkok", which is running daily from 10am to 9pm, until Oct 25.

data.title: Thai star Ray MacDonald honoured
data.description: House Samyan Cinema invites audiences to revisit the movies of a beloved Thai actor during "Tribute To Ray MacDonald", a special seven-day screening programme featuring seven films from different stages of his career.

data.title: Bangkok Climate Action Week is back
data.description: The capital will become a dynamic hub of information, connecting changemakers, local communities and global leaders to address Southeast Asia's critical climate challenges during Bangkok Climate Action Week 2026, which is running from Saturday to Oct 11.

data.title: 13 more Chao Phraya piers go under contract
data.description: The Marine Department is pressing ahead with a 200-million-baht programme to develop 29 smart piers along the Chao Phraya River in Bangkok and surrounding areas, with all due to be completed by June 2028.

data.title: Lowry: A talent written in the stars
data.description: I met Shane Lowry during the 2010 Czech Open when I was coaching at Celadna, the host club. He was a fresh-looking 23-year-old relaxing outside the scorer's office with a grin on his face like a Cheshire cat. He had good reason to smile as he had just shot a stunning second round 64!

data.title: Sharpening creativity
data.description: Satit Kalawantavanich is a legendary graphic designer and the founder of Sam Noh, a graphic design studio, and Phenomena, a renowned advertising and film production house. He is also the creator of Propaganda, an iconic design brand famous for its playful signature character Mr.P. In his 60s, Satit established Studio Avocado which provides creative and strategic consultancy.

data.title: 4 NHA condo projects get nod
data.description: The government on Tuesday approved four apartment projects by the National Housing Authority (NHA), offering more opportunities for low-income people to access high-quality housing at a reasonable price.

data.title: Cops nab 2 for arson attack
data.description: Police have arrested a Turkish man, 31, and his ex-girlfriend, 40, a former sales manager, over an arson attack on a company in Bang Khae district of the capital.

data.title: PP demands QR codes off list ballots
data.description: People's Party (PP) list MP Parit Wacharasindhu has called for barcodes to be removed from party-list election ballots after the Constitutional Court ruled that their use was constitutional but warned that such markings could undermine public confidence in the secrecy of voting.
